planting.note: Direct sow onto bare, thin mineral soil over exposed limestone in fall so the seed germinates with autumn rains and overwinters as a low rosette; avoid mulch or any amendment that would let competing vegetation shade out the seedlings.

directions: Leavenworthia stylosa is a diminutive winter annual confined almost entirely to a handful of limestone cedar glades in Tennessee's Central Basin and the adjoining Kentucky Pennyroyal, germinating with autumn rains directly on bare, mineral soil over exposed bedrock. Its basal rosette of lobed leaves overwinters close to the ground, then in March and April sends up short flowering stems topped with small four-petaled blooms ranging from pale lemon-yellow to white. Like its glade-cress relatives it completes its entire life cycle before the shallow glade soil bakes dry and hard in early summer, setting seed and vanishing until the following fall. In cultivation it needs the same stark, undisturbed, lime-rich microhabitat as its wild glades, with no mulch or groundcover competition for the tiny seedlings.

planting.note: Direct sow onto thin, mossy soil pockets over exposed limestone in fall so seedlings establish a low rosette before winter, then flower in late winter to early spring; keep the site free of leaf litter and taller competing vegetation.

directions: Leavenworthia exigua is one of the smallest of the glade-cress annuals, occupying thin, mossy soil pockets over exposed limestone in cedar glades of the Nashville Basin and scattered barrens farther west. Seeds germinate in fall and the plant overwinters as a low rosette before producing slender flowering stalks in late winter to early spring, each tipped with small pale lavender-to-white four-petaled flowers typical of the mustard family. The entire visible plant disappears by early summer as the glade soil dries and heats, leaving only seed in the thin soil to begin the cycle again the following autumn. Because it cannot tolerate shading or competition from taller vegetation or leaf litter, it should be sown onto bare rocky ground that mimics the open, scoured nature of its native glade habitat.
